newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST - Barclays profits up, buy-back seen.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Barclays profits up, buy-back seen.

text.p: Barclays Plc, parent of Barclays Bank and investment bank BZW, looks set to announce a healthy rise in pretax profits next Tuesday boosted by good growth in consumer lending led by Barclaycard.
But the market will be looking just as closely for a further buy-back of shares to add to the more than one billion stg Barclays has spent on repurchases in the last 18 months.

Analyst's forecasts for the bank's 1996 pre-tax profits range from 2.34 to 2.45 billion stg, with a dividend of 30.5 to 32.5p per share, after 2.083 billion stg and 26p respectively for the previous 12 months.

Most analysts expect further share repurchases -- Barclays is certainly generating enough capital to be able to spend around 600 million stg this year -- but some are beginning to feel that it may not be the best course for much longer given the large rise in Barclays' share price.
Barclays was the top performer in share price terms in the banking sector last year. The price gained 35.4 percent and outperformed the FTSE Allshare index by 11.7 percent.
Robert Law, banking analyst at Lehman Brothers, said he saw a special dividend a better way of enhancing shareholder value as banks' return on equity is likely to erode in coming years.
In any case, Law's projections assume a return of capital to shareholders of 400 million stg at the full-year stage and a further 600 million stg over the next year.
John Leonard, banking analyst at Salomon Brothers, sees some 625 million stg of available capital in 1997 after dividends have been paid and 500 million stg has been earmarked for growth.
Leonard also expects a buy-back to be announced next week and said his initial reaction to the idea of a special dividend was negative because of the bad tax implications for many investors.

In Barclays' core businesses, analysts will be looking closely at the performance of its investment banking unit BZW, with most expecting it to have had a marginally less profitable second half, characterised by lower trading and commission income and high costs.
Partly offsetting these factors, Barclays Global Investors, the bank's asset management business, is thought to have improved its performance in the second half.
Another feature is likely to have been solid growth in consumer lending including credit cards with rather less spectacular growth in mortgages.
